datasets.title: Somalia - 2013 Tropical Cyclone 03A path and impacts
datasets.description: Track of Tropical Cyclone 03A, which formed over the Indian Ocean off the north-east coast of Somalia and moved towards the coast in November 2013, with the position, maximum sustained wind speed and minimum pressure at each six-hourly point. The description of the source also reports the impacts: wind speeds of 74 km/h (46 mph) and 100 to 200 mm of rain caused flooding and gale force winds in Puntland, with loss of lives and the destruction of livestock, fishing boats, settlements, service centres, roads, schools, and communication and electrical installations. The most affected areas included Dangorayo, Bandar Beyla, Garowe and Eyl districts, and coastal villages in Bari region including Hafun, Iskushuban, Bargal, Qandala and Allula districts. An estimated 142,380 persons were affected, with 8,523 households worst hit and 1,435 households having lost all their livestock, and approximately 80 deaths were reported, mostly of children and the elderly. Water sources were flooded or contaminated. FAO estimated that 800,000 livestock were in the affected area, with anecdotal evidence of a survival rate below 10 per cent in the hardest hit areas. [Source: merged from the records of the same layer on the Humanitarian Data Exchange (HDX) and the ICPAC Geoportal]
datasets.details: The layer holds the track points of the storm; the impacts are only reported in the text of the source. HDX dates the dataset to November 2010, but the track points are from November 2013.

resources.title: 2013 Tropical Cyclone 03A Path CSV
resources.description: CSV file. This layer shows the movement path of Tropical Cyclone 03A. 2013 TC03A formed off the north-east coast of Somalia across the Indian Ocean, moving directly towards the coast of the country in the following days. The storm produced a wind speed of 74 kph (46 mph) and (100-200)mm of rain. It caused heavy rains with flooding and gale force winds in the Somali region of Puntland.
